subject: Urban Planning
title: Venice: Loved to Death
description: A short lesson to help you apply Venice: Loved to Death.

hook.text: Venice had 175,000 residents in 1951. Today, fewer than 50,000 remain. Tourism is killing the city.

buildup.text: 30 million tourists visit annually — 600 times the resident population. Cruise ships erode the lagoon's foundations.

discovery.text: Apartments become Airbnbs. Grocers become mask shops. The city functions only for visitors, not residents.

twist.text: Venice finally banned large cruise ships in 2021 and started charging day-trippers an entry fee in 2024.

climax.text: MOSE flood barriers now protect against tidal flooding. But no barrier stops overtourism from hollowing the city.

punchline.text: The water may not sink Venice. The tourists might.

quiz.question: How has tourism affected Venice's resident population?
options: It grew thanks to tourism-related jobs and investment
It declined from 175,000 to fewer than 50,000 as apartments became rentals
It stayed stable because residents benefit from tourist spending
